render_policy: Where the `render` block was and was not applied. `render.hgt_cm` only bites when the bag's HEIGHT axis is the variable one, and in this brand it usually is not. (a) OMITTED on everything zipped, magnetic or moulded - the whole MidLoader / TopLoader / FastFuel / Tubular / Aero Wedge / DynaPack / MTX group - because the height is fixed by a zip line or a rigid shell. (b) OMITTED on the roll-tops whose roll runs along LENGTH rather than height: the BackLoader and BackLoader X seat packs roll at the tail, the FrontLoader and RackLoader roll at both end caps, the two fork bags roll at the top of an axis that lies along the fork leg, and the Wedge DryBags roll at the tail. Their published heights are fixed cross-sections and need no override; where their LENGTH figure is the extended one that is said in dims_note instead, since the spec gives no render.len_cm. (c) APPLIED to three products only: BarLoader, Pannier DryBag 16 L and Pannier DryBag 24 L. All three roll down a VERTICAL axis, so the height is the variable one; in each case Topeak already publish the rolled-shut figure rather than an unfurled one, and the render block records that finding with its evidence so that a later pass does not read those heights as unfurled and stretch the bags upward. No Topeak product needed an estimated-from-photo render height. One candidate, the RackLoader DryBag, looked at first like a case where the drawn height should be lower than the published one; measuring its two orthographic studio views showed the real problem was a transposed axis in the source data, which was fixed in dims_cm instead - see that record.
notes: Topeak is the odd brand out in this catalogue: roughly half of these products are STRUCTURED - injection-moulded mounting hardware, rigid EVA foam shells, welded TPU panels that hold their own shape - and must not be rendered as slumped fabric sacks. The three mounting families a builder has to know are (1) QuickClick / Fixer, a moulded male rail on the bag that slides into a bolt-on or clamp-on female bracket (DynaPack DX uses Fixer 7 on the seatpost, Wedge DryBag S/M use F25 on the saddle rails); (2) MTX QuickTrack 2.0, a long moulded plate on the underside of the bag that slides fore-to-aft into a matching Topeak rack rail and locks - MTX bags cannot mount on anything else; (3) the plain hook-and-loop / Omni Strap soft mounts used by the bikepacking Loader line. Where an axis follows a tube rather than a world direction the mount.axes block says so (along_toptube, along_forkleg). Topeak's own spec strings are consistently ordered LENGTH x HEIGHT x WIDTH - that is verified against six separate product pages in this brand - and every dims_cm below is decoded on that basis.

mount.notes: Strapped down onto a rack platform with two Omni Straps - no bracket, no rail, so it works on almost any front or rear rack including the Topeak TetraRack. On a REAR rack the barrel runs fore-and-aft (len = -x, as recorded). Topeak's own on-bike photograph shows it on a FRONT rack with the barrel running ACROSS the bike instead; a builder targeting the front-rack case should read len as z. Needs a rack of some kind; it cannot mount to a bare frame.
